t: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of accounting standards as listed in the material?
e: Benefits listed are uniformity, reliability, comparability, assistance to auditors and measuring management performance; profitability is not guaranteed.

t: AS 1 deals with:
e: AS 1 is Disclosure of Accounting Policies; AS 2 is stock valuation, AS 3 cash flow and AS 9 revenue recognition.

t: A large fire claim occurs on 10 April, after the balance sheet date but before the accounts are approved. Which standard governs its treatment?
o: AS 4 – Events occurring after the balance sheet date
e: AS 4 deals with events occurring after the balance sheet date and whether they require adjustment or disclosure.

t: A small unlisted insurer contends that segment reporting under AS 17 does not apply because its turnover is below the threshold. The correct position is:
o: AS 17 is not applicable to insurers at all
AS 17 applies only if turnover exceeds ₹500 crore
AS 17 applies only to listed insurers
AS 17 applies to all insurers irrespective of listing and turnover requirements
e: For insurers, AS 17 Segment Reporting applies regardless of the listing and turnover criteria in the standard.

t: Which standard enjoys a partial exemption from application as noted in the material?
e: The material notes a partial exemption from application of AS 12 Government Grants.

t: Recognising expenses when incurred rather than when paid follows the:
e: Under the accrual principle, revenues and expenses are recognised when earned or incurred, not when cash moves.

t: Providing for probable losses on doubtful outstanding premium while not anticipating unrealised gains reflects the:
e: Conservatism (prudence) requires anticipating losses but not gains.

t: If capital is ₹300 crore and liabilities are ₹1,700 crore, total assets as per the accounting equation are:
e: Assets = Capital + Liabilities = 300 + 1,700 = ₹2,000 crore.

t: Which section of the Companies Act, 2013 requires every company to have a Board of Directors?
e: Section 149 provides that a company shall have a Board of Directors.

t: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is governed by which section of the Companies Act, 2013?
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 deals with CSR; 138 is internal audit, 149 Board of Directors and 177 Audit Committee.

t: Internal audit is mandated under which section of the Companies Act, 2013?
e: Section 138 deals with internal audit; Section 177 deals with the Audit Committee.

t: KMP, a term used in the Companies Act and accounting, expands to:
e: KMP refers to Key Management Person(nel) such as the CEO, CFO and Company Secretary.

t: NCLAT stands for:
o: National Corporate Litigation and Arbitration Tribunal
e: NCLAT is the appellate body over NCLT (National Company Law Tribunal).

topic: Supplement: Insurance Act and IRDAI Rules
t: Under Section 64VB of the Insurance Act, 1938, an insurer may assume a risk only when:
o: The premium is received in advance or guaranteed to be paid in the prescribed manner
The proposal form is signed by the proposer
The policy document has been issued
The agent has collected the premium cheque
e: Section 64VB prohibits assumption of risk unless the premium is received in advance or is guaranteed/deposited as prescribed.

t: Pass book shows a favourable balance of ₹3,20,000. Cheques issued but not presented ₹60,000; cheques deposited but not collected ₹45,000; interest of ₹5,000 credited by bank not recorded in the cash book. Balance as per cash book is:
From 2018, Ind AS adoption was widened to NBFCs having net worth:
o: More than ₹250 crore but less than ₹500 crore
e: The 2018 phase covered NBFCs with net worth of ₹250 crore or more but below ₹500 crore, besides all listed companies.

t: IFRS 17 deals with:
o: Insurance contracts of an insurer and reinsurance
e: IFRS 17 (and Ind AS 117) covers accounting for insurance and reinsurance contracts.

topic: Supplement: Insurance Act and IRDAI Rules
t: Under Ind AS 117, the simplified Premium Allocation Approach (PAA) is typically available for contracts with a coverage period of:
o: Any period, at the insurer's option
e: PAA is permitted for short-duration contracts (coverage of one year or less) or where it approximates the general model, making it relevant to most general insurance business.

t: Available Solvency Margin is ₹2,700 crore and Required Solvency Margin ₹1,500 crore. The solvency ratio is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Solvency ratio = ASM / RSM = 2,700 / 1,500 = 1.80.

t: Under the IRDAI (Actuarial, Finance and Investment Functions of Insurers) Regulations, 2024, Schedule I relates to:
e: Schedule I covers actuarial functions; finance is Schedule II and investment Schedule III.

t: A premium cheque is received on 25 March for a policy whose risk incepts on 10 April. In the accounts for the year ending 31 March, the amount is shown as:
o: Premium received in advance under current liabilities
Gross direct premium of the current year
e: Where the inception of risk falls outside the accounting period, the amount is premium received in advance and is a current liability.

t: Gross claims paid ₹500 crore and reinsurance recoveries on claims ₹120 crore. Net claims paid are:
e: Net claims = gross claims less reinsurance recoveries = 500 − 120 = ₹380 crore.

t: Net claims paid ₹380 crore; net outstanding claims (including IBNR) at year end ₹640 crore and at the beginning ₹600 crore. Net Incurred Claims are:
e: Net incurred = 380 + 640 − 600 = ₹420 crore.

t: Net Written Premium ₹2,400 crore; opening UPR ₹1,300 crore; closing UPR ₹1,200 crore. Net Earned Premium is:
e: A release of UPR adds to earned premium: 2,400 − (1,200 − 1,300) = ₹2,500 crore.

t: A premium receivable under PMFBY from the State Government has been outstanding for 300 days. For solvency purposes it is:
o: Admissible, as the limit for government-sponsored schemes is 365 days
Valued at zero, as the limit is 180 days
Valued at zero, as the limit is 30 days
e: Premiums receivable under State/Central government sponsored schemes are placed at zero only if not realised within 365 days.

t: A balance of ₹15 crore due from a foreign reinsurer with no branch in India has been outstanding for 200 days. For solvency computation the amount is:
o: Admissible in full, as reinsurer balances are always admissible
Valued at zero, as the limit for such reinsurers is 180 days
Valued at zero, as the limit is 90 days
Admissible in full, as the limit is 365 days
e: Reinsurers' balances other than Indian reinsurers and foreign reinsurers with branches in India are placed at zero if outstanding beyond 180 days.

t: Listed equity shares costing ₹120 crore have a fair value of ₹150 crore on the balance sheet date. The ₹30 crore difference is:
o: Credited to the Fair Value Change Account under equity
Credited to the Profit and Loss Account
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Unrealised gains or losses on actively traded equity are taken to the Fair Value Change Account, not to profit.

t: Which of the following assets is placed at zero value for solvency computation regardless of age?
o: Furniture, fixtures, dead stock and stationery
e: Furniture, fixtures, dead stock, stationery, deferred expenses and fictitious assets are placed at zero value.

t: RSM 2 is determined as:
o: 30% of the higher of Gross Incurred Claims × Factor B and Net Incurred Claims
20% of the higher of Gross Incurred Claims × Factor B and Net Incurred Claims
e: RSM 2 (claims basis) is 30% of the higher of gross incurred claims multiplied by Factor B and net incurred claims.

t: Gross Incurred Claims × Factor B = ₹1,100 crore and Net Incurred Claims = ₹1,250 crore. RSM 2 is:
e: RSM 2 = 30% of the higher amount, 1,250 × 30% = ₹375 crore.

t: For a line of business RSM 1 is ₹420 crore and RSM 2 is ₹450 crore. The RSM for that line is:
e: RSM is the higher of RSM 1 and RSM 2 for each line, so ₹450 crore.

t: ASM ₹1,800 crore and RSM ₹1,350 crore. What is the insurer's position vis-à-vis the regulatory control level?
o: Ratio 1.50, exactly at the control level
e: 1,800 / 1,350 = 1.33, which is below the 150% control level of solvency.

t: The AS 3 cash flow statement provides information about historical changes in:
e: AS 3 deals with historical changes in cash and cash equivalents classified into operating, investing and financing activities.

t: Net written premium of the Fire segment during the preceding twelve months is ₹400 crore. Under the percentage method the UPR for Fire is:
e: Segments other than Marine Hull carry UPR at 50% of net written premium: 50% × 400 = ₹200 crore.

t: An annual policy with net premium ₹36,500 incepted on 1 January. Under the unexpired-period (1/365) method, the UPR at 31 March (90 days expired, non-leap year) is:
e: Daily premium ₹100; unexpired days 365 − 90 = 275; UPR = 275 × 100 = ₹27,500.

t: Premium shall be recognised as income:
o: At the end of the policy period
On the date the proposal is accepted
Over the contract period or the period of risk, whichever is appropriate
e: Premium is recognised as income over the contract period or period of risk, whichever is appropriate.

t: Deduction for health insurance premium under Section 80D for an individual below 60 years (self and family) is up to:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹25,000; ₹50,000 where the insured is a senior citizen; an additional ₹25,000/₹50,000 for parents.

t: Unlisted equity securities and those not actively traded are measured at:
o: Fair value through profit and loss
e: Unlisted and not actively traded equity and derivatives are carried at historical cost.

t: Loans made by an insurer are measured at:
o: Fair value at balance sheet date
Historical cost subject to impairment provisions
Present value of future cash flows
Lower of cost and market value
e: Loans are measured at historical cost subject to impairment provisions.

t: An insurer's office building carried at ₹80 crore is revalued to ₹110 crore. The ₹30 crore increase is:
o: Taken to equity under Revaluation Reserve
Credited to the Fair Value Change Account
Credited to the Profit and Loss Account
e: Changes in carrying amount of real estate are taken to equity under the Revaluation Reserve.

t: Insurers are required to maintain investment accounts separately for:
e: All insurers must maintain separate investment accounts for shareholders' and policyholders' funds.

t: An amount retained for diminution in the value of investments, where the amount cannot be determined with substantial accuracy, is a:
e: A provision is an amount retained for a known liability or loss whose amount cannot be determined with substantial accuracy.

t: Form B-PL is the:
e: Form B-PL is the shareholders' Profit and Loss Account.

t: Under the Health segment, separate schedules are prepared for which sub-segments?
e: Health is split into (a) Health, (b) Personal Accident and (c) Travel sub-segments.

t: Third-party insurance is compulsory for a motor vehicle used in a public place under which section of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 146 makes TP cover compulsory; Section 164 fixes no-fault compensation (₹5 lakh death / ₹2.5 lakh grievous hurt).

t: Outstanding claims including IBNR ₹3,000 crore; URR ₹2,500 crore; Catastrophe reserve ₹100 crore; Premium deficiency ₹50 crore; other liabilities ₹400 crore; other assets ₹300 crore. Policyholders' Funds are:
Which of the following is NOT a permitted purpose for loans to full-time employees of an insurer?
o: Purchase of a car or two-wheeler
Construction of a house for personal use
e: Permitted purposes are vehicle, computer/electronics, furniture, house, children's education, festival advance and other Board-approved purposes.

t: Minimum paid-up equity capital for a general insurance company is:
e: General insurance, life insurance and standalone health insurers require ₹100 crore minimum paid-up capital.

t: An insurer's foreign branches write gross premium of ₹300 crore. The additional allowable expenses of management on this account are:
e: 10% of gross premium written outside India by foreign branches or IFSC is additionally allowed: 10% × 300 = ₹30 crore.

t: Net premium ₹1,500 crore; gross direct premium income ₹1,900 crore; reinsurance accepted ₹100 crore. Net retention ratio is:
e: Net retention ratio = 1,500 / (1,900 + 100) = 75%.
